The greater lesson from his house’s survival

Firefighters spray water along the edge of a burnout operation during the Creek Fire in California. Credits - Wikipedia

Their home remained standing

Within minutes, a wildfire can alter the surroundings of a house. Strong winds and exceptionally dry conditions drove the Creek Fire through the foothills north of Los Angeles on December 5, 2017. Burning embers were carried ahead of the main fire and ignited secondary fires around buildings, endangering homes in and around Kagel Canyon.A neighbour warned Wood Grigsby, who had lived in upper Kagel Canyon for about 12 years, about the fire while he was asleep. When he got outdoors, he discovered that surrounding properties were already in danger and that flames were spreading throughout the canyon. In contrast to nearby properties, his house was somewhat protected. Grigsby had cleared brush around the house and replaced some vegetation with gravel, reducing the fuel immediately surrounding the property.As the fire advanced, Grigsby and his son started to move furniture off the porch and look for embers and spot fires. As surrounding homes burnt, they spent hours fighting tiny fires around the property. One house was demolished about 180 feet up the hill from Grigsby’s dwelling. The Creek Fire burnt 15,619 acres in Los Angeles County and destroyed 123 structures, including 60 homes, according to CAL FIRE figures reported the week it burned.The blaze began at about 3:44 a.m. near Kagel Canyon, in the Angeles National Forest area, and grew during a time of extreme wildfire weather. in Southern California, when high winds may quickly spread fires through dry vegetation and carry burning material over the region. But for those who lived in the canyon, the threat wasn't only the main wall of fire. As foliage and structures were burnt, it generated embers that might be blown through the air and land on properties some distance distant. These embers can then spark fires in grass, leaves, landscaping material, fences or other combustibles.Those small fires matter because wildfire researchers have found that homes can catch fire through several different channels. A dwelling need not be located in the primary fire front. Research by the National Institute of Standards and Technology found that firebrands, or smouldering embers, can ignite mulch near a structure, depending on their size and number, airflow, and the moisture of the material. Researchers looked at firebrands, or smouldering embers, and how they can ignite fires in mulch near structures. Their investigations demonstrated that igniting depended on the size and number of firebrands, airflow and the moisture level of the material. Once the spark ignites a tiny fire close to a house, the risk might rise quickly. A burning piece of landscaping material could send flames to siding, decks or other combustible portions of a building.One big benefit Grigsby had before the fire came was that there was less flammable foliage just around the house. He'd cut the undergrowth surrounding the place and put in gravel instead of letting the plants grow right up against the building. So when embers landed, they had fewer fuels to catch fire with and travel to the structure. This form of planning is frequently referred to as constructing defensible space. The underlying principle is to eliminate as many flammable items around the house as possible, reducing the likelihood of the fire and embers coming into contact with the structure. 2019 study by Alexandra Syphard and USGS scientist Jon Keeley, published in the journal, offers wider context. The researchers analysed building inspectors' reports for more than 40,000 wildfire-exposed structures across California between 2013 and 2018, comparing homes that survived with those destroyed. Statewide, structural characteristics explained more of the difference than defensible-space distance did, though destroyed homes were over-represented in the dataThe most consistently important features were enclosed eaves, vent screens and multi-pane windows. These elements may reduce the chance of wind-borne embers entering a building. Multi-pane windows can also provide added protection from radiant heat. The authors also noted a limitation: many homes with more than 30 metres of defensible space or fire-resistant materials were still destroyed. That means no single preparedness step will ensure a house survives a big wildfire.Controlled wildfire studies further highlight the importance of material right adjacent to a home. In a separate NIST investigation, scientists tested several types of mulch beside realistic-scale building corners and exposed the area to showers of firebrands. The experiments found that firebrands could first create smouldering ignition in mulch, which could then transition to flaming. Under the tested wind conditions, flames from the burning mulch eventually ignited the adjacent building assembly.The results help explain why the few feet around a house can be so important in a wildfire. A fire doesn’t have to look like a single big flame front. An ember can fall on a flammable item, ignite it and then offer the following step towards the building. Grigsby and his son weren't trying to stop the fire; they were guarding against exactly this kind of ember ignition. But Grigsby's story is not to suggest that homeowners should stay and fight an advancing wildfire. Conditions near a fire can change rapidly, and skilled firefighters risk a lot even with training, protective equipment and communication systems.What made Grigsby’s experience remarkable was that his house survived as homes around him burnt. But the fact of one house cannot be reduced to one deed. The state of the property before the fire was significant. The house's structure was important. The wind direction and the severity of the fire also played a part, as did the behaviour of embers and the presence or absence of flammable material surrounding the structure.A USGS study supports that point. In their analysis, structural traits were a crucial factor in explaining which California homes survived. But the researchers also observed that the criteria they analysed could not account for all structural loss. Thus, Grigsby’s efforts during the fire represented only one part of the story. Vegetation clearance ahead of time to reduce fuel and gravel made a less flammable surface. Moving furniture away from the house removed another probable ignition source. The Creek Fire demonstrated how a neighbourhood can swiftly become a series of distinct fire environments. One property burns, while another adjacent one survives. An ember falling harmlessly on gravel can ignite a hazardous fire on dry grass or combustible landscaping.The bigger lesson is not that householders can safely fight a wildfire on their own. The wildfire survival starts before the flames arrive. Building design, ember resistance, vegetation management and removal of flammable debris can influence what happens when a wind-driven fire hits a town. Grigsby's house was one of those that survived, a reminder that a wildfire's effect on a home depends on more than whether flames reach the building.
Article Summary: Strong winds and exceptionally dry conditions drove the Creek Fire through the foothills north of Los Angeles on December 5, 2017. Burning embers were carried ahead of the main fire and ignited secondary fires around buildings, endangering homes in and around Kagel Canyon. Researchers looked at firebrands, or smouldering embers, and how they can ignite fires in mulch near structures. Once the spark ignites a tiny fire close to a house, the risk might rise quickly.

Article Title: Jiya Joshi was rejected from volunteering at a nursing home at 14; she later built a lifesaving 500-student senior care movement
Article Text:
A love lost too soon

Filling the void

Within two years of service, Jiya has helped 4,000 seniors, built a network of more than 70 youth volunteers and spread the initiative in more than 11 countries through an ambassador program.

Poll Vote & Share your view How important do you feel it is to connect younger generations with seniors? Very important Somewhat important Not important at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A generational movement

Jiya Joshi lost her beloved grandmother at 14 and decided to volunteer at a nursing home. But getting rejected from there inspired her to begin a movement uniting generations through friendship, compassion and caring.Jiya was only two when her grandparents arrived from India to Texas, to help care for her while her parents were at work. Her grandmother, Saroj, drove her to school and cooked her the most delicious snacks. Her entire day was wrapped around them and the two formed a close bond, sharing long conversations about life, school and friends.When she was in third grade, her grandparents returned to India, but distance only made the heart grow fonder, and they spoke on the phone regularly once a week.The year she turned 14, Jiya lost her grandmother, whom she called 'Dadi' and the loss left an aching void inside her, often leaving her feeling lonely. While she had her parents and friends to talk to, it wasn't the same. They didn't carry the same wisdom and gentle kindness as her grandmother did.This is when an idea struck. “What if I visit a nursing home? Maybe the residents would enjoy a visit as much as I would?” she asked.Jiya decided to volunteer at a nursing home and after being put on hold several times, she finally reached the nursing home volunteer coordinator: "I want to volunteer and visit," she explained, as per a report by Woman's World.The administrator was welcoming until she learnt Jiya was only 14. “We don’t allow volunteers under 18,” she declared. “Our staff doesn’t have time to care for both children and our seniors.”Jiya's heart was crushed, and not just due to the rejection. There was also the lingering grief of having lost one of her favourite people in the world, her Dadi. After several more refusals to volunteer, she decided to do something different.“Could I come just once — a trial visit?” she asked Sharon Williams, Activities Director at Houston’s Landon Ridge Assisted Living. “If it doesn’t work, I won’t bother you again.” Williams was touched by the girl's sincerity and decided to agree. "Let's give it a try," she said and Jiya was over the moon.Jiya arrived for her first visit at the centre with a box of supplies. She approached a group of seniors in a recreation area, put on a bright smile and introduced herself. “I’m Jiya. Would you like to paint with me?” “I love painting!” exclaimed a woman named Betty and soon she was regaling Jiya with incredible tales of her years as a nurse in Vietnam.“I was a pilot fighting the Germans in World War II,” said a second resident, and a third rushed off and returned with a chunk of concrete. “You mentioned Germany; this is part of the Berlin Wall, a piece of history,” she explained.As the word of a youthful stranger spread, residents who rarely left their rooms came out to see what the excitement was about. By the end of her visit, Jiya had made a dozen new friends and spread even more smiles. “I’ve never seen them so active,” Sharon marvelled as she helped Jiya pack up. “You’re coming back, right?”Jiya returned every Saturday that summer. While the residents loved having such a lively young person around to hold conversation and company with, Jiya loved their stories and affectionate hugs.When school started again, Jiya invited her friends to join her and many of them said yes. The teens visited in pairs and after a few outings, many told Jiya, "This is the most fun I've had volunteering."It was one invitation from Betty that caught her by surprise. "Betty asked me to keep her company at the senior home’s 4th of July event because she did not have any family to eat with her at the event," Jiya shared. This is when she thought about how many seniors were in need of active company. Roughly one in four Americans aged 65 and older is socially isolated, and 30–35% of seniors report feeling lonely at least some of the time. This isolation is linked to serious health risks, including higher rates of depression, heart disease, stroke, and cognitive decline.As interest spread, Jiya founded a youth-led non-profit organisation, Young and Old United, a movement that allowed teens to volunteer at elder care facilities while spreading love and support among hundreds of seniors across Houston.Generations were united through the feelings of friendship, compassion and care. Within two years of service, Jiya has helped 4,000 seniors, built a network of more than 70 youth volunteers and spread the initiative in more than 11 countries through an ambassador program. Together, they have raised $9,000 through local fundraisers and grants and partnered with dentists to obtain dental kits to include in hygiene kits.Hundreds of middle and high school students have begun making regular nursing home visits across the state. She mobilises youth volunteers to assemble and personally deliver hygiene kits to isolated and underrepresented seniors, offer spa days to senior women, and conduct senior interviews. YOU has also won thousands of dollars in grants from Youth Service America, AmeriCorps, and H.E.B and has an ongoing partnership with staff from United Airlines, providing hygiene kits.“Their eyes light up when they see her coming,” said Sharon. "My grandmother was a bright personality. She was a safe space where I could talk about anything. Then, when she left my life, I sought to regain the strongest connection I had ever built by reaching out to seniors within my own neighbourhood," Jiya told Bold Journey.“Our seniors still have so much to offer,” Jiya insists. “My grandmother taught me that. I can feel her smiling down on me!”Jiya hopes to help more than 3000+ seniors in 2026.
Article Summary: Jiya Joshi lost her beloved grandmother at 14 and decided to volunteer at a nursing home. But getting rejected from there inspired her to begin a movement uniting generations through friendship, compassion and caring. She has helped 4,000 seniors, built a network of more than 70 youth volunteers and spread the initiative in more than 11 countries through an ambassador program.

Article Title: 'Raaton par bhi haq hai hamara'
Article Text:
DU students marched from Miranda House to Faculty of Arts in North Campus on Monday demanding safe spaces for women in the city

Emotions and energy at the site were high as students came together in large numbers, some attending a protest for the first time

A symbol of freedom atop the statue pedestal

Making a statement of fearlessness and freedom, students climbed the pedestal of Vivekananda’s statue in the Faculty of Arts

As students came with hope, many questioned why there is still a need to fight for basic fundamental rights

‘It is sad that we still have to protest on this issue’

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe protests are effective in promoting women's safety? Yes, they raise awareness No, they don't lead to change 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The protest saw displays of slogans against patriarchy and misogyny, with chants like “narivaad zindabad” and “ek kachori do samosa, inn mardon ka kya bharosa?”

Men were present as silent supporters

While the march was open to women and queer people, male students joined but were away from the crowd





Despite a heavy downpour, Delhi University students took to the streets on Monday afternoon, marching from Miranda House to the Faculty of Arts to demand safer public spaces for women. Angered by the rising incidents of violence against women – the Aastha Kunj park alleged gang-rape being the most recent – the protestors did not mince their words with slogans and posters. “Imagine your behen beti first”, “Raaton par bhi haq hai hamara,” “Cursing is a cultural shock, but rape is not?” – these words screamed on handwritten posters, some of which were made inside metro coaches and at Vishwavidyalaya Metro station. The students also added internet culture with clock it gestures and posters that said “The baddest b***h ain’t in LA, we are here in India fighting for rights.”Making a statement of fearlessness and freedom, students climbed the pedestal of Vivekananda’s statue in the Faculty of Arts. Arshia Chakravarti, a third-year Political Science student at Rajdhani College, held a poster which read ‘Bas bohot hogaya’. “Since I’m in an off-campus college, I’ve always seen the core North Campus students climb up the Vivekananda statue pedestal (during protests). I come from West Bengal, so I have the utmost respect for him. I’ve grown up learning about his ideology. The first thing that I had to do was touch his feet, take his blessings, and then I went up there to propagate what I have learned.Being up there, I felt like I have never felt more alive and empowered,” she told us.Anisha Prabeel, a UPSC aspirant from Jharkhand, shared, “I come from a rural setup in Jharkhand, and there are so many girls dreaming of coming to Delhi to study and work toward their future, but the way things are happening, their parents are scared to send them. Even our parents worry; we haven’t told them that we are going to a protest. If we cannot ensure the safety and security of women in one of the top universities in the country in the capital, then I believe women would have no place to go. Ab yeh bilkul nahi chalega. Women ko unki azaadi aur safety milni chahiye. This generation is here to fight against patriarchy.”Emotions and energy at the site were high as students came together in large numbers, some attending a protest for the first time. Holding a placard which read, “It’s not a women’s safety issue, it’s a male violence issue”, Dharmishtha Sharma, a second year Journalism student at Kalindi College, told us, “It feels empowering to be at an all-women protest but it’s sad that we still have to do this. I have a friend in LSR, and all I felt was anxiety and terror when the case near the college came to light. At my college also, there have been many cases of stalking and harassment, so more than anything, I just feel anger. Protests absolutely make a difference – umeed pe duniya kayam hai aur hum bhi issi liye yahan hain. There is strength in numbers. If more of us show up, the louder our voice will be. We understand the power of voices. Cheenti akeli ho toh kuch nahi kar sakti lekin agar ek jhund mein aaye toh cheetiyan haathi ko bhi utha sakti hain.”As students came with hope, many questioned why there is still a need to fight for basic fundamental rights. Sanjana, a PhD scholar, noted, “All women have faced some form of harassment in their lives. It’s beyond frustrating, I am at a loss for words. Mujhe pata nahi ki kisi ke andar itni entitlement kahan se aati hai ki woh kisi ko aise ghoor sakta hai, haath laga sakta hai, humein abhi yeh basics sikhane padenge. And it is a drawback of our education system also which majorly lacks sex education. School mein hi ladko aur ladkiyon ko itna segregate karke rakhte hain ki vahin se problem start hoti hai.”While the march was open to women and queer people, male students joined but were away from the crowd. Adnan, a first-year master’s student at Department of History, shared, “Yeh maine pehla protest dekha hai jo sirf girls lead kar rahi hain aur bahut achcha lag raha hai unki energy ko dekh ke. Hum protest mein aaye hain as supporters. Hum door se unka hausla badha rahe hain. Jo recent incidents huye hain, woh hum mein se hi koi hain toh hum bheed mein ghus ke unki awaaz nahi chheen rahe hain. Yeh issue gender se bada hai aur hum sabko uske support mein khada hona chahiye.” Another male student, who’s pursuing master’s at the Department of History, said, “Agar mard bhi protest mein hissa lete toh woh zyada aa jate, overshadow karte iss cause ko.” He added that the protest is against crimes and in favour of safety for women, not an anti-men protest.
Article Summary: Despite a heavy downpour, Delhi University students took to the streets on Monday afternoon. They marched from Miranda House to the Faculty of Arts to demand safer public spaces for women. Angered by the rising incidents of violence against women, the protestors did not mince their words with slogans and posters.

Article Title: Theatre review: Ham MacLear’s life, reimagined through Shakespeare’s words
Article Text:
A still from the play

Hamlet

The Tragedy of Ham MacLear

Hamlet

The Merchant of Venice

-Anvita Singh

Want us to review your play? Mail us at tims.delhitimes@timesofindia.com





Amid the dim lighting, actor Mantra Mugdh, playing Busker, enters the stage wearing a mask of Shakespeare. He sits down on a wooden box and begins to play an instrument shaped like a regular household utensil. The image is colourful yet ominous, like witnessing the start of something dangerous but human. A tragicomedy, if you will.And right on cue, a character named Chorus appears, whose chirpy voice and tap dancing shift the atmosphere, making it considerably lighter. Together, they narrate the tale of Ham, an old man whose love for both Shakespeare and theatre has brought them together.The narrative technique of theatre within a theatre is a clever hat tip to Shakespeare’s, but the device here also allows the play to blur the line between the story being performed and the tragedy unfolding within Ham’s life.is the account of an ailing man who attempts to rediscover his love for the timeless plays of the Bard with the help of his friends. Tightly placed at 65 minutes, the drama demands your unwavering attention as it moves seamlessly from the present to the onset of Ham’s dementia on stage, when he begins performing a scene fromin the middle ofThis is where director and lead actor Akash Khurana sparkles.His confident demeanour of a man who knows his play inside-out transforms in mere seconds into a confused performer who cannot comprehend why his loving audience is suddenly booing at him and his crew.Busker and Chorus inform us that Ham’s condition worsened after the death of his wife Desdemona, who, it is revealed later, had cheated on him with Busker.The climax mirrors the third act of a typical Shakespearean play, where a key conflict plays out in all its glory. The segment serves both as a revelation and a redemption arc, where Ham begins to navigate his own loss through Shakespeare’s words.There are several things that the production does right besides the acting, where actor Garima Yajnik dazzles as she sings and dances her way into the audience’s heart. The music, sometimes performed onstage by Mantra Mugdh as he drummed a vessel or used a singing bowl instrument, worked well with the play’s mood.The lighting was especially impeccable, helping create the eerie atmosphere during the concluding part of the drama. However, the standout part was when Ham stopped performing Shakespeare, but rather seemed to process his grief through the playwright’s work
Article Summary: is the account of an ailing man who attempts to rediscover his love for the timeless plays of the Bard with the help of his friends. Tightly placed at 65 minutes, the drama demands your unwavering attention as it moves seamlessly from the present to the onset of Ham’s dementia.

Article Title: Absent during Beed collector’s drought review, Kaij tehsildar stripped of charge
Article Text:
Beed district collector Vivek Johnson

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Sending a stern message to officials amid the drought crisis, the Beed district administration has stripped the Kaij tehsildar of his charge after he was found absent during the district collector’s visit to review the situation on Sept 26.District collector Vivek Johnson issued the order on Monday night. The naib tehsildar will hold additional charge, subject to the approval of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar divisional commissioner, until further orders.Johnson cited the officer’s apparent lack of seriousness at a time when drought mitigation requires continuous coordination and close monitoring on the ground.“The tehsildar’s absence could affect the implementation and review of essential drought-mitigation works. It was, therefore, necessary to ensure that a competent officer was available to handle these responsibilities,” Johnson said.The order does not suspend or dismiss the tehsildar. However, taking away his charge is being seen as a stern administrative response as authorities race to implement drought-relief measures across the district.The tehsildar is the key coordinating officer at the taluka level for implementing and monitoring drought-relief measures.The action followed a drought review meeting chaired by Kaij BJP MLA Namita Munde during the collector’s visit.The move has also put the administrative machinery on notice in the drought-hit region. All 11 talukas of Beed district are among the 74 of Marathwada’s 76 talukas where drought has been declared after Trigger I was invoked.
Article Summary: The Kaij tehsildar was found absent during the district collector’s visit to review the situation on Sept 26. District collector Vivek Johnson cited the officer's apparent lack of seriousness at a time when drought mitigation requires continuous coordination and close monitoring on the ground.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: LPG leak triggers blast at Sanpada snacks shop in Navi Mumbai, 2 injured
Article Text:
A LPG cylinder leakage caused a blast at a Sanpada snacks shop on Tuesday morning.





NAVI MUMBAI: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in sector-1, Sanpada on Tuesday morning. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.Purushottam Jadhav, Divisional officer of Vashi fire station said, "At 6.13 am, the Vashi fire station received the emergency call informing about a cylinder blast at a snacks shop in Pratik CHS on sector-1, Sanpada. The fire bridge team reached the spot within 5 minutes.It was found that the blast was due to leakage in one of the three LPG cylinders kept at snacks shop. The two men working at the snacks shop sustained severe burn injuries and were rushed to NMMC hospital, Vashi. Those injured were identified as Arjun Yadav (46) who has sustained 75 precent burn injuries and Manish Yadav (26), who has sustained 90 percent burns.The blast even caused damage to two shops adjacent to the snacks shop and three other shops in the neighbouring Abhimanyu CHS. While, the glass facade of Suraj hospital located opposite to Pratik CHS was shattered due to the impact of the blast."
Article Summary: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in Sanpada. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.

Article Title: 16 years after construction, KDMC mayor finally moves into civic bungalow
Article Text:
The bungalow was constructed in 2010.





KALYAN: Sixteen years after it was constructed, the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s (KDMC) new mayoral residence at Adharwadi finally got its first regular occupant, with mayor Harshali Chaudhari-Thavil performing the vastu shanti puja and entering the bungalow on Wednesday.The bungalow was constructed in 2010. However, a dispute over access to the property kept the residence largely unused for years. Several mayors subsequently attempted to resolve the road issue, but the efforts failed as villagers whose land was required for the access road were reportedly unwilling to part with the land.Even after the civic body spent lakhs of rupees on repairs, the bungalow remained unused. Former mayor Vinita Rane had performed a puja at the residence but chose not to stay there.With prolonged neglect, wooden furniture inside the bungalow was damaged and several portions were affected by termites. The civic administration later undertook extensive repairs to make the premises habitable again.After taking charge as mayor in February, Thavil took up the long-pending access issue. As she travels daily from Titwala to Kalyan, she personally held meetings with villagers and discussed their concerns. Following the resolution of the issues, the access road was finally constructed, paving the way for the mayoral residence to be used.After the road was made accessible and the neglected bungalow was completely repaired, Thavil finally entered the Adharwadi residence on Wednesday, bringing an end to the 16-year wait for the civic property to be put to its intended use.
Article Summary: Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s new mayoral residence at Adharwadi finally got its first regular occupant. Mayor Harshali Chaudhari-Thavil performed the vastu shanti puja and entered the bungalow on Wednesday.

Article Title: First 41 cattle drowned, then milk output plunged, now urad crop lost: Dharashiv family waits for aid
Article Text:
The damaged cattle shed outside his home is an even more painful reminder.





PIMPALGAON (BHUM, DHARASHIV): The walls of Vishwanath Daatkhile’s (56) house in Pimpalgaon village in Bhum tehsil of Dharashiv district bear the marks of the devastating flood Banganga river caused on Sept 22 last year.The damaged cattle shed outside his home is an even more painful reminder. Bent steel pipes, broken tin sheets and bricks are scattered where 41 cattle, 27 lactating cows and 14 calves, were once sheltered.The river rose quickly and swept away the animals that Daatkhile had reared over two decades. A year later, he said he received Rs 2.25 lakh for six cows, three registered in his name and three in his brother, Gowardhan’s . But the family has not received full compensation for the rest.A fresh govt resolution providing for full compensation to farmers in Dharashiv and Solapur who lost cattle has been issued. Despite follow-ups with the district administration, additional assistance has not come.“My son Praveen pursued it for a few months but gave up. We cannot wait forever. Otherwise, we will never come out of these losses,” Vishwanath said.Dharashiv collector Keerthi Pujar said, “We will prepare a fresh proposal as per the new GR released by govt for the flood-affected districts. The family will get the help soon.” He added that he would look into why the family did not receive the assistance despite the revised provisions.Before the flood, the Daatkhile family produced around 200 litres of milk every day. They have rebuilt part of the herd, but milk production is 40-50 litres a day.“My parents and uncle do not show their pain and financial stress to us. They are determined and confident that they will earn it back. But it is tough,” Praveen said. He works at a medical store run by a relative in Pune.He said his father had started with a single cow and gradually built the herd to 41 animals. “It was two decades of hard work. Now, it is difficult to buy big cows. A good-quality lactating cow costs more than Rs 1 lakh. We do not have that money,” Praveen said.The family recovered when people responded after reports of their losses appeared in the media. “More than govt, people helped us. They donated clothes, grain and cans of water. A group of schoolchildren from a neighbouring village who brought us a special kit at night, despite the rain,” Vishwanath recalled.With some Rs 5 lakh from public donations, Vishwanath has bought seven cows over the past year. “Rearing cows is my passion. I cannot live without them. We are coming back to normalcy,” he added. His brother, who lost 20 goats in the flood, has purchased 10 goats.But the cattle shed has not been built. Vishwanath has not been able to bring himself to reconstruct it. “I did not feel like raising it again. The panicked mooing of the cows as they were swept away before me that night haunts me. I don’t feel like putting up a new shed in the same place,” he said.The flood also destroyed a part of the family’s grape plantation. The family expected to rebuild its agricultural income after the flood, but the current year has brought another challenge, a prolonged gap in rainfall.Praveen said the family’s two-acre urad crop is lost because of inadequate rainfall. “We cultivated green chillies using borewell water. But rising temperatures and lack of rainfall have resulted in disease infestation. The production will not even be 50%,” he said.For Praveen, the flood also destroyed a personal dream. After completing his D Pharm in 2022, he planned to set up a medical store in Bhum town, the tehsil headquarters. He identified a location and purchased furniture too. The floodwaters damaged and swept away some of it. He is now trying to save enough money to restart his plan.For Vishwanath, the seven cows now represent the beginning of another long rebuilding process. His brother’s 10 goats serve a similar purpose. His two dogs, which survived the flood from the gushing waters, remain with him.As Vishwanath talks about the night of the disaster, he pulls the dogs close and gently strokes their backs. “They are now happily living with us.”
Article Summary: The walls of Vishwanath Daatkhile’s house in Pimpalgaon village in Bhum tehsil of Dharashiv district bear the marks of the devastating flood Banganga river caused on Sept 22 last year. Bent steel pipes, broken tin sheets and bricks are scattered where 41 cattle, 27 lactating cows and 14 calves, were once sheltered.

Article Title: Worker shot dead at water filter plant near Shirur
Article Text:
A representational photo of a dead body

Pune:





Two motorcycle-borne men shot dead a worker (39) at a water filter plant in Karegaon in Shirur taluka around 6:30 am on Tuesday.The Pune Rural police identified the deceased as Hamja Usman Shaikh, who was residing in Karegaon and hailed from Parbhani district. The police have also been investigating the motive behind the killing.“We have formed teams to trace the assailants. Shaikh had been working at the plant for the last six months and resided near the facility,” said Kumar Kadam, inspector of Ranjangaon MIDC police.Around 6:15 am on Tuesday, Shaikh arrived at the plant. Soon after, a woman noticed him lying on the premises and alerted his wife. The family initially thought that he might have slipped and took him to a nearby hospital, Kadam said.“Doctors declared him dead. We received a call from the hospital, and our team reached there to examine the body,” Kadam said.“We found the wounds suspicious. There were two wounds on the head—one entry and one exit—indicating that he had been shot,” the officer said.Kadam said police also found an empty cartridge on the premises of the water filter plant. Some residents also said they heard a sound resembling a firecracker around 6:30 am, Kadam said.“We then checked the CCTV footage and found two motorcycle-borne men were near the plant. The pillion rider shot Shaikh when he was starting the plant and fled,” Kadam said.The officer said Shaikh had no previous criminal record. His family members and neighbours described him as a gentleman. “Our investigation is underway,” the officer said.
Article Summary: The Pune Rural police identified the deceased as Hamja Usman Shaikh, who was residing in Karegaon and hailed from Parbhani district. Shaikh had been working at the plant for the last six months. The police have also been investigating the motive behind the killing.

Article Title: Minor raped by cop, gets pregnant
Article Text:
Nagpur:





A 25-year-old constable, attached to Quick Response Team (QRT), has been charged with allegedly raping a 17-year-old Class 12 student. The constable first contacted the girl on Instagram and later called her to his house.The accused, Prateek Dharpal, a resident of Mahesh Nagar on Borgaon Road, was named in an FIR registered at Gittikhadan police station after the girl was found to be pregnant. He was arrested earlier this week.According to the complaint, Dharpal first messaged the student on Instagram in 2022. He later asked for her mobile number and continued to chat with her on social media.Trusting Dharpal as he was a policeman, the girl agreed to meet him. On Aug 17, Dharpal invited her to his house on the pretext of his birthday. Once she was alone with him, he allegedly demanded sex. When she refused, Dharpal allegedly forced himself on the girl.The survivor did not immediately report the crime, fearing repercussions as Dharpal served as a cop. The rape came to the fore on Sept 22 when the student fainted in her school. The teachers took her to hospital, where doctors informed her parents that she was pregnant.The survivor narrated the ordeal to her parents, who approached Gittikhadan police station. Police registered a case and later arrested Dharpal.
Article Summary: Prateek Dharpal, a 25-year-old constable, has been charged with allegedly raping a Class 12 student. The constable first contacted the girl on Instagram and later called her to his house. Once she was alone with him, he allegedly demanded sex and when she refused, he forced himself on her.

Article Title: Esteban Ocon confirms Haas exit in an emotional statement, F1 future remains uncertain but not over
Article Text:
Esteban Ocon (via Getty)

Esteban Ocon could turn to Mercedes reserve role after Haas exit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Esteban Ocon will leave Haas at the end of the 2026 Formula One season. However, the French driver has insisted that his departure does not mean the end of his F1 career. Ocon confirmed the news after two seasons with the American-owned team.Ocon has already admitted that finding another full-time drive for 2027 will be difficult. Most teams have their driver plans taking shape, while Aston Martin closed one potential route after Fernando Alonso extended his stay. A reserve or test role could therefore become an option.Esteban Ocon confirmed his Haas departure in a social media statement.“My time with Haas F1 Team will come to an end at the end of the 2026 season. I leave this project with my head held high and proud of my performances in what were not always the easiest of circumstances for various reasons and factors outside of my control,” said Ocon on social media.“There are still many races to go this season and, as always, I will give it my everything behind the wheel for myself and for my team. I am still motivated. I am still hungry. This is absolutely not the end of my Formula One career”, he added.Haas also confirmed that Ocon will leave after the season. The team thanked the Frenchman for his contribution during his time with the outfit.Ocon joined Haas after a difficult final period with Alpine. Team principal Ayao Komatsu had known the driver since his early F1 testing days and believed his experience could help Haas move forward.Ocon scored points during his first season with Haas. However, he finished behind rookie teammate Oliver Bearman in the 2025 championship. Komatsu later admitted that the team had “expected more” from Ocon.Haas have also tested several young drivers as they assess their options for 2027. Ferrari-backed Brazilian Rafael Camara has emerged as a leading candidate. Leo Fornaroli, Ryo Hirakawa and Jack Doohan have also been evaluated.Bearman is expected to remain with Haas for another season. That leaves one seat potentially available, with Camara strongly linked to it.For Ocon, a reserve role could provide a route back onto the grid. He already spent 2019 as Mercedes’ reserve and third driver after losing his place at Force India.Ocon remains determined to continue racing in F1.“I will keep pushing as much as I can. I’ve won in every category I’ve driven, I won in go karts, I won in Formula Renault, I won in GP3, I won in Formula 3, I won in Formula 1. I can fight out there, I got what it takes and the hard work that I put in is… You know, you came to many places to see me work and I put the work out there, I just don’t sit around and think I have done enough, I want to do more”, he wrote.His immediate future remains unclear. But Ocon has made it clear that he intends to remain involved in Formula 1 beyond the end of his Haas contract!
Article Summary: Esteban Ocon will leave Haas at the end of the 2026 Formula One season. Ocon confirmed the news after two seasons with the American-owned team. The French driver has insisted that his departure does not mean the start of his F1 career.

Article Title: Trapped hand, speeding SUV and desperate climb: How cops stopped gutka-laden vehicle
Article Text:
Head constable, M Velmurugan, claimed that the chase started at Vilankurichi and he clung on to the SUV till Karumathampatti, which is about 40km away.

,





COIMBATORE: A police head constable foiled an attempt by three smugglers to escape in a gutka-laden sports utility vehicle, by clinging to the top of the vehicle on Avinashi Road till a highway patrol team intercepted the gang at Karumathampatti near here on Sunday morning.Head constable, M Velmurugan, claimed that the chase started at Vilankurichi and he clung on to the SUV till Karumathampatti, which is about 40km away. The three smugglers have been arrested.Acting on a tip-off, a police team led by Kovilpalayam sub-inspector Vignesh and head constable Velmurugan attempted to stop the SUV (KA 05 NG 7692) at Vilankurchi near Kovilapalayam around 5.45am.Velmurugan climbed atop the SUV when the driver slowed the vehicle but refused to halt and sped towards Avinashi. The constable clung atop the SUV by holding the roof rails of the vehicle despite the smugglers driving the vehicle athigh speed.Vignesh immediately informed the Karumathampatti police and highway patrol team on Avinashi Road, who chased the vehicle for nearly an hour and eventually intercepted it at Karumathampatti and saved Velmurugan without any injuries.Police found more than 100kg of gutka products in the car and identified three smugglers travelling in the car as P Babu Dhara, 27, A Rajesh, 23 and S Suresh, 20, all from Rajasthan.They were smuggling the contraband from Karnataka to Coimbatore. Police seized the contraband and the car.Meanwhile, prohibition and excise minister K Vignesh and minister for backward classes welfare RS Rajakannappan spoke to Velmurugan over a video call and congratulated him for his bravery.They said they would take Velmurugan’s daring act to the attention of chief minister C Joseph Vijay.Later, Velmurugan told TOI“When we approached the vehicle, the driver stopped and rolled down the window. While we were questioning the occupants, he started moving the car and closed the window, trapping the SI’s hand inside. Our SI ran for a few metres with his hand trapped inside. Luckily, the SI fell on the road without any injuries, but I climbed atop the SUV. I realised the suspects should not be allowed to escape, so I held on to the rails tightly till they were captured. As police personnel, we were just doing our duty.”
Article Summary: Head constable, M Velmurugan, claimed that the chase started at Vilankurichi and he clung on to the SUV till Karumathampatti, which is about 40km away. The three smugglers have been arrested. Police seized the contraband and the car.
